evals.prompt: Audit https://github.com/flathub/org.freedesktop.Sdk.Extension.node24/pull/44 for a multi-branch rollout. Do not modify GitHub or the current checkout. Determine the exact cherry-pick chain each branch/* ref needs, identify branches that must be skipped, and save an actionable rollout report containing commit IDs, PR links, target bases, and the validation you would run before asking me to publish.
evals.expected_output: A repository-backed rollout analysis that uses original focused PR commits, finds a contiguous version chain rather than copying branch/25.08 wholesale, inventories all branch/* refs only, and includes a publication approval gate.
expectations: The report audits all and only branch/24.08, branch/25.08, and branch/26.08, recording each target head or an equivalent immutable base identifier.

The exact oldest-first chain is b49f9d62acd6cb59dbc85209195b514269a0538f then 72d05933de199cdd17fc905da3f254c3d2791d20 for branch/24.08 and only 72d05933de199cdd17fc905da3f254c3d2791d20 for branch/26.08.
The report links predecessor PR #39 and reference PR #44, uses original update commits rather than merge commits, and excludes closed unmerged PR #38 from the chain.
branch/25.08 is skipped as already current, and branch/26.08 is recognized as intentionally using runtime-version 26.08beta rather than divergent.
The validation plan covers diff scope, branch identity, YAML/XML parsing, source checksum, release ordering and uniqueness, clean state, and unchanged remote target heads.
Local full Flatpak builds are not required before requesting publication approval; compilation is delegated to per-PR Flathub builds unless the user separately asks for local builds.
The report contains an explicit publication approval gate and the audit performs no GitHub or checkout mutation.

evals.prompt: Using the supplied local git fixture, propagate the reference Flatpak dependency update to every branch/* branch by cherry-picking. One target has a manifest conflict because its runtime-version and build options differ. Resolve it without losing target-specific settings, prepare local commits and patches, validate the declared source checksum and release metadata, and stop before any push. Save a rollout report explaining the conflict resolution. Fixture setup instructions are in the input file.
evals.expected_output: All fixture branch/* targets are classified; outdated targets receive the verified update while runtime-specific settings survive the conflict, checksums and release history validate, and no remote publication occurs.
expectations: Exactly branch/24.08 is prepared; branch/25.08 and branch/26.08 are classified as already current.
The branch/24.08 result preserves branch 24.08, runtime-version 24.08, strip true, and prepend-path /usr/lib/sdk/example/bin while updating only release intent.
The declared local source archive exists and its measured SHA-256 equals the manifest checksum.
Release 1.1.0 dated 2026-02-02 and release 1.0.0 dated 2026-01-01 each appear exactly once in newest-first order, and XML parsing passes.
A non-empty patch and verifiable local git artifacts are saved for branch/24.08, with a clean completed repository.
The report accurately discloses whether Git naturally produced the fixture's predicted conflict and explains how target-specific settings were preserved.
No push, pull request, or GitHub mutation occurs.
